claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has excellent mechanical strength at 1600 °C.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has poor room-temperature ductility.
Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has good or predicted irradiation resistance.
Replacing approximately 5 at% Mo with Zr will produce beneficial lattice distortion in NbMoTaW.
Zr has a large atomic radius that can generate local lattice strain when incorporated into a multicomponent alloy.
Zr-induced lattice distortion increases the spread of dislocation cores in NbMoTaW.
Zr-induced lattice strain and altered dislocation cores lower the Peierls barrier in NbMoTaW.
Lowering the Peierls barrier will facilitate room-temperature dislocation motion and improve ductility.
Zr is refractory and has a high melting point.
Minor Zr substitution will preserve the single-phase BCC structure and high-temperature integrity of NbMoTaW.
The Zr-modified alloy will have greater room-temperature plastic strain and less brittle fracture than untreated NbMoTaW.
The Zr-modified alloy will retain mechanical strength comparable to untreated NbMoTaW at 1600 °C.
The Zr-modified alloy will retain irradiation resistance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
Lattice distortion and compositional complexity can alter irradiation-defect formation energies, migration barriers, diffusion pathways, and interstitial-vacancy recombination.
Zr-induced lattice distortion will preserve, rather than adversely alter, the irradiation-defect dynamics of NbMoTaW.
Hot rolling and related thermomechanical treatment can improve ductility and help retain a BCC structure in a Zr-containing multicomponent alloy.
Excess Zr or unsuitable processing may form deleterious secondary phases and compromise performance.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to compositions and processing conditions that maintain a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure and allows excessive substitution to fall outside scope, whereas the falsification rule broadly treats secondary-phase formation in the 3–7 at% test series as falsification. This could classify an explicitly out-of-bound composition, such as 7 at% Zr, as a decisive test.
